title: katG and inhA
dek: Two INH stories. katG S315T is activation loss, high-level, ETH often spared. inhA promoter-up is more target, low-level, ETH cross-resistant. Coding inhA is rarer.
story: Isoniazid is a prodrug. KatG catalase-peroxidase activates it; the INH–NAD adduct inhibits InhA (FAS-II enoyl-ACP reductase). Loss of activation and overexpression/alteration of the target are genetically different resistances with different MICs and different ETH implications.

katG S315T is the global high-level allele: enough residual catalase to keep fitness, not enough INH activation. Ethionamide uses EthA, then InhA, so S315T often remains ETH-S. inhA promoter mutations (c-15t, t-8c, …) increase InhA abundance: low-level INH-R, ETH cross-R. Coding inhA (S94A, I21T) is less common but sits on the same target.
Other INH-associated genes (ahpC promoter compensatory, ndh, kasA) are catalogue footnotes, not Xpert substitutes. Report the allele class, not “INH-R” as a Boolean.
deep: MTBDRplus probes katG 315 and inhA promoter. It will miss uncommon katG loss-of-function elsewhere — those tend to be unfit and rarer in transmission, but they exist.
ahpC promoter-up is often compensatory for katG loss, not a primary INH mechanism to treat as the cause.
High-dose INH in some MDR recipes is a bet on inhA-only low-level R. S315T does not pay that bet.
Numbering: inhA promoter positions are relative to the start; do not confuse c-15t with codon 15 of InhA.

visual.caption: Two loci, two mechanisms. katG codon 315 is the high-level hotspot. inhA promoter sits upstream of the coding target that ETH shares.

example.title: Both alleles in one BAM
example.setup: katG S315T AF 0.95 and inhA c-15t AF 0.20.

steps.title: High-level INH is already decided
steps.body: S315T at fixation is high-level INH-R. The promoter minority does not make it “low-level.”

steps.title: ETH is now also in trouble
steps.body: The inhA promoter minority may be enough to spoil ETH even though S315T alone would not.

steps.title: Report both with AF
steps.body: This is evolution in one patient, not a parser bug.

example.takeaway: When both INH mechanisms coexist, believe the more severe INH phenotype and the ETH cross-R.

choices: Low-level INH-R with obligatory ETH cross-R
High-level INH-R via failed activation, ETH often still an option genetically
